children: New Delhi, Oct. 26 -- Actor Sonu Sood is set to earn Rs.3.52 crore in rental income over five years after leasing a commercial property in Mumbai's Versova area to coffee business Bokka Coffee. The agreement, registered in October 2026, provides for a gradual increase in monthly rent, allowing the actor to generate a growing stream of income from the property.
According to The Economic Times and Hindustan Times, citing property registration documents reviewed by Square Yards, the commercial unit is located in Aram Nagar, Versova, in Andheri West.
The deal adds to Sood's commercial property investments, which include a separate unit leased to HDFC Bank in Mumbai's Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC).

The agreement starts with a monthly rent of Rs.5 lakh for the first year. That amount will increase annually, reaching Rs.6.8 lakh a month by the fifth year. The lease structure means Sood's rental income will rise over time rather than remain fixed throughout the agreement.
The rental agreement provides for an annual escalation of approximately 8%. The monthly payments are scheduled as follows:

By the final year, the monthly rent will be around 36% higher than it was at the beginning of the lease. The total rental value over the five-year term is estimated at Rs.3.52 crore, according to the documents.
The agreement also includes a security deposit of Rs.32 lakh. Stamp duty of Rs.93,000 and registration charges of Rs.1,000 were recorded as part of the transaction.

Commercial property can offer investors a relatively predictable income stream through long-term leases, particularly when tenants are contractually committed to paying rent and the agreement includes scheduled increases. However, returns depend on factors such as the property's purchase price, maintenance expenses, taxes, vacancy risks and other ownership costs.

Sood's Versova transaction follows another commercial leasing deal earlier in 2026. He leased a roughly 2,700-square-foot unit at Trade Centre in BKC to HDFC Bank, with the starting monthly rent fixed at Rs.11.75 lakh under a nine-year agreement.
That lease provides for a 15% increase after each successive three-year period.
The two agreements use different escalation structures. The Bokka Coffee lease raises rent annually, while the HDFC Bank agreement increases it at three-year intervals.

Aram Nagar, in Mumbai's western suburbs, benefits from access to commercial districts, residential neighbourhoods and entertainment industry hubs. The wider Versova area is connected through Link Road, SV Road and the Western Express Highway, with metro and suburban railway access nearby.

For Sood, the Bokka Coffee agreement adds another source of rental income alongside his acting career. The Rs.3.52-crore figure represents the projected rent across five years, not a guaranteed investment profit or the property's market value.
